_README: Rider ids that are variants of one person, and the id they belong to. CONSULTED AT INGEST: without this a re-ingest recreates every absorbed id straight from the scrape files, because the files still carry the old spelling — the same way the Dorsal placeholders came back. Lives outside the DB for that reason, like stage_notes.json and route_type_overrides.json. Produced by audit_rider_duplicates.py + merge_rider_duplicates.py; every entry carries the evidence for the claim, because a merge IS a claim and a wrong one fuses two careers invisibly. The `separated` section is the MIRROR of `aliases`: pairs a human examined and ruled DIFFERENT people. Without it audit_rider_duplicates.py re-proposes them on every run and the next --apply quietly re-merges a decision somebody already made.

rider/aaron-gammell.evidence: Unbound 2010/2011/2012, one rider. Two of his three registrations spell it GAMMEL (2011, 2012) against one Gammell (2010), so the source majority picks the canonical, not string length. A separate Jed Gammell rides Chequamegon with the double L and is a different person.

rider/andrew-lesperance.evidence: 21 of his 22 gravel registrations across 8 races spell it L'Esperance; one Leadville 2023 entry drops the apostrophe. PCS's own slug is andrew-l-esperance and Canadian Cycling Magazine confirms a single rider from Nova Scotia.

rider/greg-follett.evidence: Leadville 1997 and 1999, one rider — the organiser's own All Time Finishers list carries both his rides at times that match this database to the second (9:14:34 in 1997, 8:26:54 in 1999), same state, same M2 category. RESOLVED 2026-09-11 by counting EVENTS rather than records: Leadville 1997 spells it FOLLET and Chequamegon 1999 spells it Follet, against Follett at Leadville 1999 — 2 events to 1. The Leadville PDF is not an independent witness, it is the same Athlinks data. No outside source records him at all. Canonical greg-follet stands, now on evidence rather than on an alphabetical tie-break.

rider/mathieu-belanger-barette.evidence: Bélanger-Barrette, double R, confirmed by the UCI rider database plus Precision Hydration, Cycling Weekly, Velo, Reserve Wheels and FirstCycling. PCS spells it 'barette' and PCS IS WRONG; its slug was what link_gravel_riders matched on. The canonical therefore moves to the 0-result sportmaniacs identity, which is the only one spelling his name correctly — the opposite of what a most-results rule would pick. CONFIRMED SAME PERSON: PCS's own page for the misspelled slug gives a birth date of 3 August 1989, matching the press profile of Mathieu Bélanger-Barrette exactly. PCS has only the one page — /rider/mathieu-belanger-barrette is a 404 — so this is a single rider whose NAME PCS has wrong, not two riders. The upstream typo cannot be fixed from here and is recorded in DATA_SOURCES.md.

ernest-gilioli|ernest-gillioli.evidence: Wikipedia's 1926 Tour startlist has Gillioli at number 147 as a touriste-routier; its 1909 list has Gilioli at 157 as a lone rider. Two entries, two numbers, two categories. PCS dates Gilioli to 1885, making him 41 in 1926 — possible, but nothing asserts one man.

giuseppe-bereta|giuseppe-beretta.evidence: Il Lombardia 1909 and Milan-San Remo 1934: 25 years, two different races, nothing in between. Placing 72nd in a professional classic at about 49 is not credible.

gilbert-desmet-i|gilbert-de-smet-ii.evidence: They share 93 stages and nobody rides a race twice. PCS's roman numerals separate two riders of one family; the hyphenation differs as well, which is why the name heuristic called them SAME.
gilbert-desmet-i|gilbert-de-smet-ii.note: never merged — refused by the share-a-stage test
